recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Any future desire for explicit Slot.location or a different simple-client scheduling model should be handled through a new work-group decision rather than as remaining FHIR-9209 application work.
issue_request: FHIR-9209 asked for Slot to include a location for which an appointment can be scheduled. The Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution instead chose to change Schedule.actor from 1..1 to 1..* so a Schedule can define a composite such as practitioner plus location, or HealthcareService.
initial_application: Commit d2764d2195090a391e6f845f8297b869f59fbe8a applied Trackers# 9209 and 9270 to the legacy spreadsheet source, changing Schedule.actor from 1..1 to 1..* and adding grouped-resource guidance. Commit 58402c6ae49c927a3818ab2d5ca3d1cc58a0253b then added provider-plus-location Schedule narrative and examples. Commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 later converted Schedule to the current StructureDefinition/list source form.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists schedule=Schedule and slot=Slot as active resources. Current source/schedule/structuredefinition-Schedule.xml has Schedule.actor min 1, max *, target profiles including HealthcareService and Location, and a comment explaining grouped actors. Current Schedule narrative and examples describe one schedule per practitioner/location pair. Direct Zulip and Confluence searches found no FHIR-9209 discussion that changes this conclusion.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Adding Slot.location would conflict with the final modified resolution because the approved model is composite Schedule actors, and that model is already present in authoritative current source.

related_jiras.note: The same historical commit also applied separate Slot.appointmentType wording for FHIR-9270, but that issue is independent of the Schedule.actor location decision and was not decided here.
